value.body:
Prior art to check when designing (recalled 2026-11-14, not verified against current docs). Jack Heart: "this is somewhere where Slurm, Ray, and other sweep tools, and job management tools, probably have something to teach us". Closest match: Dagster sensors — a function evaluated repeatedly returns RunRequest(run_key=...); only unseen run_keys launch. Kubernetes controllers: reconcile desired against observed from current state (level-triggered), watches plus periodic resync, objects deduped by name. Snakemake checkpoints: the DAG is re-evaluated after a rule finishes; its rerun-on-code-change trigger was contentious. Slurm: static dependencies at submit (--dependency=afterok, job arrays), no re-evaluation. Ray Tune: an in-process event loop with scheduler callbacks, not declarative. Lessons to test: dedupe by an author-controlled name (address) rather than a content digest; poll first, subscribe later; decide what a pass does with failed jobs and with jobs that drop out of the list (never cancel implicitly).
